description.p: KEMU is a traditional, direct-to-QEMU desktop frontend for Linux, built with Qt 6 Widgets and KDE Frameworks 6 for desktop integration. It provides a simple and intuitive graphical interface to manage local virtual machines.

ul.li: Create, edit, and delete QEMU virtual machines
Integrated D-Bus viewer with audio and clipboard sharing
Support for the SDL display backend
Hot-swapping of ISO and floppy images
User-mode networking, plus rootless virtual networks
Portable VM storage: VMs are stored as self-contained directories with relative start scripts
Export and import VMs as compressed archives (.kemu.tar.zst) for seamless backup or migration
OVA export and import for cross-platform interoperability

description.p: KEMU dropped X11 host support in favor of native Wayland, refactored the VM overview into framed detail cards alongside improved UEFI/Secure Boot firmware detection and QEMU capability probing, and added experimental dual-monitor support in a separate window.

KEMU replaced external networking helpers with an in-process virtual L2 switch, DHCP/DNS servers, libslirp backend using secure socketpairs and seccomp sandboxing, while adding LUKS system disk encryption with KWallet support, QEMU guest agent integration, multiple disks, linked clones, cloud-init/OS template management, desktop notifications, system tray/CLI launching, and dropping GTK display support.

KEMU migrated its integrated D-Bus viewer to peer-to-peer connections while removing the external dbus-daemon and SPICE viewer dependencies, centralized VM lifecycle management in VmRuntimeManager, added native Wayland pointer capture, logind power management integration, a virtual network link toggle, and non-blocking cloud-image deployments, and improved audio buffering, DMA-BUF rendering, and archive import/export handling.

KEMU split VM creation into a compact new-VM dialog and a full hardware editor, added Flatpak sandbox detection and QEMU capability probing alongside an optional SLIRP user-mode network fallback, introduced VSync-driven rendering, dirty-rect uploads, and cursor/audio optimizations in the integrated D-Bus viewer, and implemented fully asynchronous VM startup, power-off save-state handling, and VM name path-traversal protection.

KEMU promoted the integrated D-Bus viewer out of experimental status by adding relative pointer support, mouse capture mode, live CD/DVD and floppy media controls, USB device passthrough, and per-VM persisted viewer settings, alongside live QMP snapshot management, selectable input devices, persisted VM architecture metadata, and reliable OVA/OVF bootable defaults.

KEMU introduced the integrated D-Bus display viewer with HiDPI cursor scaling, clipboard sharing, and on-demand frame updates, added floppy disk image support, MS-DOS/FreeDOS templates, and Intel PRO/100 network device emulation, refactored its details view and snapshot/QEMU command management, and improved startup reliability, error handling, and single-instance enforcement.
KEMU gets Floppy disk image support, MS-DOS/FreeDOS templates, ISA-PC chipset constraints and new network devices.
Initial release featuring basic VM management and UI.
